SOURCE: "Evaluation of OpenAI o1: Opportunities and Challenges of AGI", Tianyang Zhong, Zhengliang Liu, Yi Pan, Yutong Zhang, Zeyu Zhang, Yifan Zhou, Shizhe Liang, Zihao Wu, Yanjun Lyu, Peng Shu, Xiaowei Yu, Chao Cao, Hanqi Jiang, Hanxu Chen (14 co-first authors), ... Tianming Liu. Preprint, arXiv:2409.18486v5 [cs.CL]; no venue printed. Year 2024 by arXiv ID; the page stamp reads "23 Sep 2026" (see PROBLEMS).
First-author affiliation as printed: Zhong, "Department of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences, University of Alberta, Edmonton, Canada". Most co-first authors: School of Computing, University of Georgia; CSE, University of Texas at Arlington.

COVERAGE: 281 pages, 747,242 chars. This is a partial read.
- Read in full: pp 1-3 (title, abstract), 11-34 (intro, all 27 scope/dataset subsections), 42-67 (3.9, 4.1 Test Procedure, 4.2-4.10 with their figures), 155-157 (discussion, conclusion).
- Result sections read in full (prose): 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10, 4.13, 4.17, 4.19, 4.24, 4.25, 4.28.
- Sampled (opening/closing prose, tables; case figures not read): 4.11, 4.12, 4.14, 4.15 (p100 not read), 4.16, 4.18, 4.20, 4.21, 4.22, 4.23, 4.26, 4.27.
- Keyword scan only (tables, counts, grader, caveats): pp 68-154 figure pages, appendix pp 158-266.
- Skimmed or not read: TOC pp 4-10; related work pp 35-42 (start and end only); reference list (after about p266) not read, so cited years are not verified.

CLAIMS
- claim: The benchmark is 27 tasks in five groups, each tested on a handful of items.
  number: 27 tasks
  setup: o1-preview; the authors call the set "AGI-Benchmark 1.0"
  quote: "In total, 27 tasks were designed to evaluate the model's adaptability"
  where: p12
- claim: The headline coding figure is 10 of 12 problems with three attempts each.
  number: 83.3% (10/12)
  setup: LeetCode Weekly 413, 414 and Biweekly 138; pass on any of 3 submissions; graded by LeetCode's judge; both failures "hard"
  quote: "o1-preview successfully passed 10 out of 12 problems, yielding a high passing rate of 83.3%"
  where: p46, Table 2
- claim: "100% accuracy" in high-school maths rests on 10 items.
  number: 10/10
  setup: MATH dataset, 5 algebra and 5 counting/probability, levels 1-5; selection method not stated
  quote: "achieving 100% accuracy across all 10 test cases"
  where: p91
- claim: College maths was 7 correct of 12, graded by the authors by hand.
  number: 7 correct, 1 questionable, 4 incorrect; 0/3 on advanced discrete
  setup: 12 author-written problems
  quote: "The correctness of the answers was manually determined by the authors."
  where: p99, Table 5
- claim: Radiology "ranking highest" holds for R-1 and R-L only; gpt-4-turbo and gpt-4o beat it on R-2.
  number: R-1 0.3019, R-2 0.0448, R-L 0.2841 against gpt-4-turbo R-2 0.0656
  setup: 10 reports "randomly selected" from the private SXY set (317,339 reports); ROUGE against doctors' reports; five GPT baselines; prompt tuned first ("several experiments to determine the optimal prompt phrasing", p16)
  quote: "R-1: 0.3019, R-2: 0.0448, and R-L: 0.2841, ranking highest among the six models"
  where: p49, Table 3
- claim: Other item counts are equally small.
  number: NLI 10 (2 per dataset); EHR 10; MedMCQA 10 of 194,000, "100% accuracy"; genomics 20/20; social media 11; public health 10 prompts; analogical 10 of 136; anthropology/geology 5; Cherokee 5 sentences; psychometrics 3 shown; art education 6
  setup: as listed
  quote: "We randomly selected two test samples from each dataset's test set, conducting a total of 10 test cases." (p54); "the final test consists of only five questions" (p30)
  where: pp 19, 29-33, 54, 118, 121, 141, 144
- claim: Chip design "outperforming specialized models" is a prose comparison with ChipNeMo's published sample answers, with no score.
  number: none
  setup: 6 cases (3 chatbot, 2 EDA script, 1 bug summary), judged by the authors
  quote: "we adopted the ChipNeMo [91] test sample ... as a reference framework"
  where: p72

LIMITS
- Not stated anywhere I read or scanned: access route (web UI or API), test dates, sampling settings, number of runs. Exceptions: 3 attempts for code, and one maths item "repeated a few more times" (p99). Radiology timings for six models suggest API use, but that is my inference.
- No inter-rater agreement and no intervals. Graders are the authors or unnamed "experts"; automatic grading only for LeetCode and ROUGE.
- Baselines exist for radiology (5 GPT models), chip design (ChipNeMo, qualitative) and one GPT-4o maths answer. No human baseline was measured; "human-level" and "surpassing many human experts" are not backed by any measured comparison.
- Contamination was addressed only for anthropology/geology (new expert questions, p30) and partly for college maths. Most tasks draw on public sets (MNLI, IMDB, XSum, MATH, SciQ, LogiQA, MedMCQA), yet the paper says the benchmark "resists manipulation and memorization" (p14).
- EHR items are "randomly selected" on p27 and "manually selected" on p105. The "EHR" data are OHSUMED journal abstracts.
- Several tasks report no count or score (robot planning, quantitative investing, table-to-text, 3D layout, logical reasoning, sentiment). Stochastic processes reports "80% accuracy rate on basic problems" (p111) with no n in the main text.
- For logic, the authors set aside the answer key: "the official standard answer is not necessarily accurate" (p88).
- Conceded: "Although the problem set is relatively small" (p26); "our test results are not comprehensive due to OpenAI's policy restrictions" (p118).
- Dated: o1-preview is superseded.

BUILDS ON: Chain-of-thought [193]; LLplace prompt [199]; ChipNeMo [91]; TweetEval [9]; MATH [46]; LogiQA [76]; GeneTuring [52]. Printed as numbers only; years unverified because the reference list was not read.

CODE: none worth keeping.

FIGURES: Figure 1, p15, "Schematic Overview of the Evaluation Methodology": shows the 27 tasks in five groups. Weak candidate; Table 2 (p46) and Table 5 (p99) explain the sample-size problem faster.

PROBLEMS: The page-1 stamp reads "arXiv:2409.18486v5 [cs.CL] 23 Sep 2026", which is inconsistent with a 2409 ID unless v5 is a late revision; confirm before citing a date.
